patch.objective: Selecting a throttling strategy and bandwidth allocation

sources.cite: AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Associate (SAA-C03) exam guide (PDF): Design Secure Architectures 30%, Design Resilient Architectures 26%, Design High-Performing Architectures 24%, Design Cost-Optimized Architectures 20%
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch of the PDF on 2026-11-17. Quoted: Task 2.1 'Determining the AWS services required to achieve loose coupling based on requirements', Task 3.2 'Decoupling workloads so that components can scale independently'; Task 1.3 'Encrypting data at rest (for example, AWS KMS)', 'Implementing access policies for encryption keys'; Task 2.2 'Service quotas and throttling', Task 4.4 'Selecting an appropriate throttling strategy'.

sources.cite: Amazon DynamoDB Developer Guide, Error handling with DynamoDB
sources.note: Read directly on 2026-11-17. Relevant text: ProvisionedThroughputExceededException, 'Your request rate is too high ... Reduce the frequency of requests using Error retries and exponential backoff', OK to retry; for BatchWriteItem, failed puts come back in UnprocessedItems, 'The most likely cause of a failed read or a failed write is throttling', 'If you retry the batch operation immediately, the underlying read or write requests can still fail due to throttling ... we strongly recommend that you use an exponential backoff algorithm'.
